column1: # ---- Source texture name (case-insensitive, * and ? wildcards)  ->  generic material id  ->  optional tint
# Most specific row wins (an exact name beats a glob; a longer glob beats a shorter one), not the first, so the
# order here is only for the reader. A tint is r,g,b (0..1) or #rrggbb and multiplies the game's texture.
# A map's own folder (MAPS/<map>/) and a cubemap suffix are stripped before matching, so never name a map here.
# Ids are generic (what the surface IS); a game draws each id from its own art. Unknown ids are drawn flat by the game.
# `python3 -I tools/bsp/bsp.py unmapped <maps>` lists every texture that hits no row below, with face counts.
# --- never drawn as a surface a player reads
# --- walls: painted plaster, worn plaster, wallpaper
# --- found by `bsp.py unmapped` over the murder maps (2026-10-20)
# --- added for zombie-zone-maps' 14 converted maps (2026-10-20): the textures its old table knew by substring, and the families of its escape and mall maps
# Space-station and film-set hull plating (a folder per set), pipes, grates and panels
# --- never a surface a player reads: sprites, screens, cables, lights
# --- generic words (2026-10-20, from `bsp.py unmapped` over ~/mapsrc): a texture is named for what it is, whatever folder the mapper put it in.
# Every glob here is shorter than the rows above, so any folder- or family-specific row still wins. Deliberately NOT mapped: brand and
# character textures (a cartoon's or a film's skin), posters and signs, arcade and shop decals, model skins (MODELS/*), swatch
# palettes (COLOR/*, COLORS_PACK/*) and developer numbers; a game that wants those draws them itself.
# --- architectural families the 35 zombie-zone maps left unmapped (2026-10-23): chateau, havana, italy, piranesi, realworld, nature
